requirement.description: The View.__init__ method incorrectly raises a TypeError when target is not a data view (line 410) instead of checking if it's a ValueCastable or Signal. This causes failures when trying to create Views from Signals.
requirement.contract: When creating a View with a target parameter, the method should accept Signals (which are ValueCastable) as valid targets, not just data views. The validation should check if the target is a ValueCastable or Signal, not just if it's a data view.

requirement.description: The View.__getitem__ method has incorrect handling for array layouts when indexing with a value. It raises a TypeError but doesn't properly validate the key type for array layouts.
requirement.contract: When accessing an array layout with a value key, the method should validate that the key is a value or value-castable object and raise a proper TypeError with a descriptive message if not. For non-array layouts, it should properly handle value indexing with a descriptive error message.

requirement.description: The View.__getitem__ method doesn't correctly handle the case where a non-value key is used for non-array layouts. It should raise a TypeError with a descriptive message.
requirement.contract: When accessing a non-array layout with a value key, the method should raise a TypeError with the message "Only views with array layout, not {layout}, may be indexed with a value".

requirement.description: The View.__getattr__ method has incorrect error handling for missing attributes. It doesn't properly format the error message to match expected format.
requirement.contract: When accessing a non-existent attribute on a View, the method should raise an AttributeError with a properly formatted message that includes suggestions for similar field names. The error message format should match the expected pattern.

requirement.description: The View.__getattr__ method doesn't properly handle reserved field names. It should raise an AttributeError when trying to access reserved names via attribute access.
requirement.contract: When accessing a reserved field name (starting with underscore) via attribute access, the method should raise an AttributeError with the message "View of {target} field '{name}' has a reserved name and may only be accessed by indexing".
